dialect.detail: Likely AcuCOBOL or Micro Focus with ACUCOBOL-style screen I/O extensions (ACCEPT with LINE/POSITION/SIZE/TAB/UPDATE/NO BEEP/CURSOR/CONTROL clauses, C$RERR call, EXC-KEY control variables). French-language business application with form-based printing via P080 subprogram.
evidence: ACCEPT ... LINE ... POSITION ... SIZE ... TAB UPDATE NO BEEP CURSOR ... CONTROL "UPPER"
COPY copybook pattern with .CPY and .FC/.FDE extensions

purpose.domain_detail: HR personnel management system - prints a list of number of persons by trade/profession (métier) with optional nationality breakdown
purpose.summary: Program 3-NATMET reads personnel registry records, accumulates counts by trade (métier) and optionally by nationality/residence, stores intermediate results in an indexed file, then prints a formatted report via a form-printing subprogram (P080). It is part of a larger French-language HR/personnel management suite.

notable_features: AcuCOBOL-style screen ACCEPT with LINE/POSITION/SIZE/CONTROL clauses
Heavy use of COPY statements (22 copybooks) for modular structure
Indexed file with DYNAMIC access and SELECT OPTIONAL
DECLARATIVES section with USE AFTER ERROR
French-language comments and box-drawing characters in comments
Form-based report printing via P080 subprogram
OCCURS on counter fields in file record
verdict.notes: Source is in Latin-1 encoding with French text and IBM box-drawing characters in comments. The dialect is likely AcuCOBOL based on screen I/O syntax and C$RERR, but Micro Focus is also possible. Many implementation details are hidden in the 22 COPY members which are not shown. The program is part of a larger suite (numbered programs, shared copybooks like V-LINK.CPY, V-VAR.CPY).
